hints.title: Monotonic Capacity Feasibility
hints.text: The answer must lie between the largest individual element and the total sum of all elements. If a candidate maximum sum is feasible, any larger candidate sum is also feasible.

hints.title: Greedy Subarray Packing Invariant
hints.text: Given a target sum cap, sequentially accumulating values into the current subarray until exceeding the cap gives the minimum count of required subarrays.

hints.title: Bisection Over Target Range Procedure
hints.text: Set the lower search limit to the maximum element and the upper search limit to the total sum. While the lower bound is less than the upper bound, evaluate the midpoint. Count the required subarrays greedily. If the count is at most k, contract the upper bound; otherwise advance the lower bound.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N log S) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Trying all ways to partition an array of length N into k subarrays requires checking combinations in exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bisection over the sum range [max(nums), sum(nums)] takes O(N log S) time and constant O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize monotonic feasibility, define the tight lower and upper search limits, and write clean greedy partitioning logic.
